origins.section: The JIT Reorders Too, So x86 Shows a Reordering Its Hardware Doesn't Make
volatile on Every Access That Needs Ordering Rules Out Both Reorderings
A Racy Reference May Expose an Object Before Its Constructor's Writes Land
Acquire/Release Orders a Handoff, Not a Write Followed by a Read

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-interpreter-clean: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-interpreter-clean: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-interpreter-clean: Option b is reachable from the page. L196-212: in mp-plain, r1=1 r2=0 occurred 0 times under -Xint and 0 times with C1 only. L214-218: with the writer in its own method, C2 alone gave 14,220 and excluding that one method from compilation gave 0. 'The reordering came from the C2-compiled writer, which intra-thread semantics allows: the two stores go to different fields.'
recorded.prompt:q-one-volatile-flag: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-one-volatile-flag: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-one-volatile-flag: Option b follows from L274-277: 'Thread 2's plain write and its read are still free to swap ... Store buffering needs each thread's write ordered before its own read, so both fields must be volatile, or both checks made under one lock.' sb-half (L267-271) shows r1=0 r2=0 in 455,114 trials. The quiz's admitting thread (plain write, then volatile read) corresponds to the page's thread 2.
recorded.prompt:q-quote-cache: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-quote-cache: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-quote-cache: Option c follows from L301-306: zero in 30,000,000 trials, but 'The JLS still allows it: the constructor's writes and the store of the reference are plain writes to different variables ... only final fields come with a guarantee for a reader that gets the reference through a race ... A zero on one machine and one JVM is not a property of the code: a weaker processor or another JIT may produce it.' Summary L366-367 says the same.
recorded.prompt:q-release-acquire-handshake: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-release-acquire-handshake: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-release-acquire-handshake: Option c follows from L343-348: 'Neither stops an acquire read from overtaking a release write that comes before it in the same thread, which is the store buffer's reordering, so store buffering failed 610,780 times.' sb-release-acquire is at L331-335, and Summary L368-369 says 'Store buffering needs volatile or a full fence.'

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-interpreter-clean:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-interpreter-clean:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-interpreter-clean:a: Refuted by L166-168: 'On x86 the buffer drains in program order ... other cores see one core's stores in the order it made them ... the swap it suffers is made by the hardware'. The page puts no condition on what code issued the stores. Summary L362-363 says the flag-before-data order is something 'the hardware alone never did'.
recorded.prompt:q-interpreter-clean:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-interpreter-clean:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-interpreter-clean:c: Refuted by L163-164: 'The caches stay coherent throughout. What hides the write is a queue in front of the cache, not a stale copy in a thread's "working memory" (unit 5.1.2).' L214-218 also places the cause in the compiled writer: excluding only the writer gave 0.
recorded.prompt:q-interpreter-clean:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-interpreter-clean:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-interpreter-clean:d: Refuted by combining two passages. L166 and L362-363 say x86 hardware keeps one core's stores in order, so timing alone cannot produce flag=true with data=0. L214-218 traces the outcome to the C2-compiled writer: excluding that method gave 0, and C2 alone gave 14,220.
recorded.prompt:q-one-volatile-flag:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-one-volatile-flag:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-one-volatile-flag:a: Refuted mainly by data. In sb-half (L267-271), thread 1 read thread 2's plain write y as 1 in 4,637,716 trials (r1=1 rows) with no lock involved. L156-159 says a buffered store drains to the cache 'a little later' on its own. L274-277 gives the real cause, the swap. No passage states directly that plain writes don't wait for a lock.
recorded.prompt:q-one-volatile-flag:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-one-volatile-flag:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-one-volatile-flag:c: Refuted by L274-277. The JMM does not stop the plain access in either thread from swapping, and one volatile field covers message passing, not store buffering. sb-half gave r1=0 r2=0 in 455,114 trials. Summary L364-365: 'One volatile field is enough to hand data over, not for a write-then-read handshake.'
recorded.prompt:q-one-volatile-flag:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-one-volatile-flag:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-one-volatile-flag:d: Refuted by the sb-half result (L267-271, 455,114 trials with both reads 0) and L274-277. The page's publication mechanism (L250-252) covers only a data write that comes before the volatile write in the same thread's program order.
recorded.prompt:q-quote-cache:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-quote-cache:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-quote-cache:a: Refuted by L301-303: 'the constructor's writes and the store of the reference are plain writes to different variables, the same freedom the JIT used on x and y above'.
recorded.prompt:q-quote-cache:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-quote-cache:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-quote-cache:b: Refuted by L196-218. On x86, the C2-compiled writer made r1=1 r2=0 visible in mp-plain (6,727 trials), so the JIT does not keep a thread's stores in order. L304-305: 'another JIT may produce it'. The option's hardware half is true (L166).
recorded.prompt:q-quote-cache:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-quote-cache:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-quote-cache:d: Refuted by L166-167: on x86 'the buffer drains in program order ... other cores see one core's stores in the order it made them', so x86 hardware does not swap two stores. The risk the page names is the JIT and weaker processors (L303-305, L170-171).
recorded.prompt:q-release-acquire-handshake:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-release-acquire-handshake:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-release-acquire-handshake:a: Refuted by L343-345: '*volatile* accesses are, in addition, totally ordered with each other'. Release/acquire lacks that, and sb-release-acquire gave 610,780 trials with both reads 0 against 0 for sb-volatile. L351-352: 'Use volatile, or a lock, when each thread writes and then reads what the other wrote.'
recorded.prompt:q-release-acquire-handshake:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-release-acquire-handshake:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-release-acquire-handshake:b: Refuted by L345-347: an acquire read can overtake an earlier release write in the same thread, 'which is the store buffer's reordering'. L156-159: a store waits in the store buffer while the next instruction runs. The 610,780 failures show the release write was not yet visible.
recorded.prompt:q-release-acquire-handshake:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-release-acquire-handshake:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-release-acquire-handshake:d: Refuted by L343-344: 'an acquire read and the accesses after it are ordered after a matching release write and the accesses before it'. That covers other accesses. mp-release-acquire (L326-330) ordered the plain x with 0 forbidden outcomes. Reference table L379 says the same.
